newsitem.title: UK: Japan thanks Britain for help in Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan thanks Britain for help in Peru crisis.

text.p: Japan thanked Britain on Thursday for its "suggestion and cooperation" in the ending of the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru.

Media reports said British security forces, including members of the SAS elite unit, played a vital role in the rescue of 71 hostages after 127 days in captivity. British hostage negotiators were also involved, the reports said.
"For the resolution of this protracted incident, the British government provided suggestion and cooperation to the Japanese government," a statement from the Japanese embassy in London said.
"Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto sent a letter to Prime Minister John Major today expressing his most heartfelt gratitude for the cooperation ..."
In December Britain said it would send "experts" to help obtain the release of the hostages being held by guerrillas at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

British officials denied on Wednesday that the SAS had been involved. It is official policy never to comment on the operations of the SAS which successfully stormed the Iranian embassy in London in 1980 where 21 people were being held hostage.
